findings.title: Action button float is ignored inside new flex container
findings.body: .small-action is now a flex container (flexbox + align-items), but its button still uses float: right. Float does not apply to flex items, so the expand/details button stays in source order immediately after .small-action-desc instead of being pinned to the right edge. The old left padding (4em) that reserved space beside the floated avatar was also removed, so this row no longer matches the previous layout in any browser that honors display: flex. Use margin-left: auto on the button (and drop the floats) if the button is meant to sit at the end of the row.

findings.title: order() maps 0-based order onto 1-based box-ordinal-group
findings.body: The new order mixin copies $val straight into -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group. Those 2009 properties are 1-based (default 1); the standard order property is 0-based (default 0). The correct prefix is $val + 1. As written, an item with order(1) shares a group with unspecified siblings in old WebKit/Firefox, and order(0) is an invalid ordinal (dropped, so the item stays at the default). Header callers pass order(2) and order(3), which currently sort the same as modern order only by luck; any 0 or 1 value will reorder .panel / .extra-info-wrapper differently in prefixed engines than in current browsers.

findings.title: align-items() emits invalid and mismatched vendor properties
findings.body: align-items() sets -webkit-box-align to the modern keyword unchanged, and also sets a non-existent -ms-align-items. The 2009 box model uses start/end/center/baseline/stretch, not flex-start/flex-end, and there is no -moz-box-align even though flexbox() sets display: -moz-box. -ms-flex-align is the only legacy align property that is real. Call sites that pass center or baseline happen to be legal for -webkit-box-align, but flex-start/flex-end (or any future caller) will be ignored by old WebKit while modern align-items still applies, so vertical alignment of the header, small-action rows, and bullet badges will differ across the browsers these prefixes are meant to cover.

findings.title: Panel right-alignment depends on auto margin that 2009 flex ignores
findings.body: .panel lost float: right and now relies on margin-left: auto plus order(3), while .contents is turned into a flex container via the new flexbox() mixin (display: -webkit-box / -moz-box / -ms-flexbox / flex). Auto margins do not absorb free space in the 2009 box model those prefixes enable, and floats on flex/box items are ignored, so there is no fallback. In engines that honor -webkit-box or -moz-box but not modern flex, the header panel (login, icons) will sit next to the title instead of on the right. .d-header .title { float: left } was removed in the same change, so the title no longer floats either when flex is absent.
